questions.question: List the seven life processes and explain each in one sentence, using a goat or a mealie plant as the example.
questions.expected_answer: Nutrition: obtaining food; the goat eats grass, the mealie makes food by photosynthesis. Respiration: releasing energy from food in the cells, using oxygen. Excretion: removing wastes made by the body, such as carbon dioxide and urea. Growth: a permanent increase in size by making new cells, such as a kid becoming an adult goat. Reproduction: producing new individuals of the same kind. Sensitivity: detecting stimuli and responding, such as the goat hearing a dog or a shoot bending to light. Movement: changing position of the whole organism or part of it, such as walking or a sunflower turning.

questions.question: Explain the difference between respiration and breathing, and between excretion and egestion.
questions.expected_answer: Respiration is the chemical process in every living cell that releases energy from food, usually using oxygen and producing carbon dioxide and water; breathing is only the movement of air in and out of the lungs in some animals to supply oxygen and remove carbon dioxide. Excretion is the removal of waste substances made by the body's own chemical processes, such as carbon dioxide and urea; egestion is getting rid of undigested food as faeces, which was never made by the body's cells.

questions.question: A car moves, uses petrol and oxygen, and gives off waste gas. Explain why it is still classified as non-living, and classify a cotton shirt, a stone and a dry seed.
questions.expected_answer: The car only imitates some processes: it cannot grow, cannot reproduce, does not obtain its own food, responds only when operated by a person, and is not made of cells; a living thing must carry out all seven processes by itself and be made of cells. A cotton shirt is once living (made from a dead plant). A stone is never living. A dry seed is living but dormant: it respires very slowly and will germinate when given water, warmth and oxygen.
